Prerequisite: Managed devices (FortiGates and other Fortinet devices, such as FortiProxy) registered and authorized over the FGFM tunnel, within the number of devices the model or license allows
What it enables: Policy package installation, device configuration revisions, install verification, terminal and FortiOS GUI access to devices, packet capture, FortiGuard package deployment, and the FortiProxy ADOM features
How to put it in place: On each device, set central management to the FortiManager's address; then authorize the device in GUI: Device Manager, and check it with diagnose dvm device list
Source: FortiManager 8.0.1 CLI Reference, "Administrative Domains" (the number of network devices depends on the model and the VM license), config system admin setting (unreg_dev_opt), and diagnose dvm device list; FortiManager 7.6 New Features Guide, "Fabric of FortiManager - License for total number of managed devices is enforced only on FortiManager Supervisor 7.6.5"; Chapter 13 rows *FortiGate-to-FortiManager (FGFM) management tunnel* and *Device registration and authorization*

Prerequisite: ADOMs enabled and created, with the devices and administrators assigned to them
What it enables: Per-ADOM administrator access and profiles, restricted and ADOM-scoped administrators, policy block permissions, the FortiProxy ADOM type, and backup ADOMs
How to put it in place: config system global; set adom-status enable; end, then create the ADOMs in the GUI and assign administrators with config system admin user; edit <ADMIN>; set adom <ADOM>; end
Source: FortiManager 8.0.1 CLI Reference, "Administrative Domains" ("Configuring ADOMs": the feature must first be enabled, ADOMs created, and administrators assigned; the number of ADOMs depends on the model and the VM license) and config system global (adom-status)

Prerequisite: FortiSwitches, FortiAPs, or FortiExtenders managed by a FortiGate that the FortiManager manages (FortiSwitches over the FortiGate's FortiLink interface)
What it enables: FortiSwitch Manager, AP Manager, and Extender Manager features: templates and profiles, RMA and replacement, imports, packet capture, firmware staging, and Fabric Authorization Templates
How to put it in place: Connect and authorize the devices on the managing FortiGate (P1), then check them in GUI: FortiSwitch Manager, AP Manager, or Extender Manager
Source: FortiManager 7.4 New Features Guide, "FortiSwitch devices can be imported from a CSV file 7.4.2" (the FortiLink interface used to allow the FortiGate to manage the FortiSwitch) and "Export Managed FortiAPs and import FortiAPs from a CSV file 7.4.2"; FortiManager 7.0 New Features Guide, "Extender Manager for central managed FortiExtender devices"; FortiManager 7.2 New Features Guide, "Fabric Authorization Template automatically provisions and authorizes LAN Edge devices on the managed FortiGates 7.2.1"

Prerequisite: The switch-controller traffic-sniffer setting on the FortiGate that manages the FortiSwitch
What it enables: Packet capture on managed FortiSwitches started from the FortiManager
How to put it in place: On the managing FortiGate, configure config switch-controller traffic-sniffer (a FortiOS setting, not a FortiManager one)
Source: FortiManager 7.2 New Features Guide, "Perform packet capture on managed FortiGate interfaces and on managed FortiSwitches 7.2.2" (FortiManager triggers packet capture on managed FortiSwitches when traffic-sniffer has been configured)

Prerequisite: Workspace mode (or workflow mode) enabled
What it enables: Automatic ADOM unlock after a policy package installation
How to put it in place: config system global; set workspace-mode normal; end
Source: FortiManager 8.0.1 CLI Reference, config system global (workspace-unlock-after-install is not available if workspace-mode is set to disabled); Chapter 13 row *Workspace mode (ADOM and policy package locking)*

Prerequisite: A workflow approval matrix for each ADOM: the approvers, and the mail server for approval notifications
What it enables: Approval of workflow sessions by the named approvers, including the CLI diff and selective approvals
How to put it in place: config system workflow approval-matrix; edit <ADOM>; set mail-server <SMTP>; config approver; edit 1; set member <APPROVERS>; end; end
Source: FortiManager 8.0.1 CLI Reference, config system workflow approval-matrix; Chapter 13 row *Workflow mode (change approval)*

Prerequisite: Reachable RADIUS, TACACS+, or LDAP servers, each with a unique shared secret or bind account, and administrator accounts that use them
What it enables: Remote administrator authentication, so the authentication server enforces password, inactivity, and lockout rules; wildcard remote administrators; and TACACS+ accounting of CLI commands, configuration changes, and logins
How to put it in place: An organization RADIUS, TACACS+, or LDAP service, then config system admin radius; edit <RADIUS>; set server <RADIUS_IP>; set secret <SECRET>; end and config system admin user; edit <ADMIN>; set user_type radius; set radius_server <RADIUS>; end
Source: FortiManager 8.0.1 CLI Reference, config system admin radius, config system admin tacacs, config system admin ldap, config system admin user (user_type, radius_server, tacacs-plus-server, ldap-server, wildcard), and config system locallog tacacs+accounting setting; Chapter 13 rows *RADIUS administrator authentication*, *TACACS+ administrator authentication*, and *LDAP administrator authentication*

Prerequisite: A SAML identity provider with the FortiManager registered as a service provider, and the IdP certificate on the FortiManager
What it enables: SAML single sign-on for administrators, with signed assertions and requests and SHA-256 or SHA-512 signatures
How to put it in place: An organization SAML IdP, then config system saml; set status enable; set role SP; set idp-entity-id <IDP_ENTITY_ID>; set idp-single-sign-on-url <IDP_SSO_URL>; set idp-cert <IDP_CERT>; end
Source: FortiManager 8.0.1 CLI Reference, config system saml; Chapter 13 rows *SAML SSO wildcard admin user to match all users on IdP server*, *SAML assertions and SAML requests can be now signed to better support third-party IdPs*, and *SAML SSO supports SHA-256 and SHA-512 for both IdP and SP*

Prerequisite: PKI: the DoD CA certificates and current CRLs on the FortiManager, and certificates from that PKI for administrators and for the FortiManager's HTTPS server
What it enables: PKI (certificate) administrator login, two-factor authentication (available only when a PKI administrator account is configured), LDAPS server validation, and a DoD-issued management server certificate
How to put it in place: config system certificate ca; edit <DOD_CA>; set ca <CA_CERTIFICATE>; end and config system certificate crl; edit <DOD_CRL>; set crl <CRL>; end (CRLs are imported, so keep them current by procedure), with certificates issued to the administrators and the FortiManager
Source: FortiManager 8.0.1 CLI Reference, config system certificate ca, config system certificate crl, config system admin user (user_type pki-auth, ca; two-factor-auth is available when a PKI administrator account is configured), and config system admin setting (admin_server_cert); Chapter 13 rows *PKI (certificate) administrator authentication* and *CA certificates and CRLs*

Prerequisite: FortiToken Cloud with a token for each administrator
What it enables: Two-factor authentication for administrators (FortiToken Cloud email, mobile, or SMS)
How to put it in place: FortiToken Cloud, then config system admin user; edit <ADMIN>; set two-factor-auth ftc-ftm; end
Source: FortiManager 8.0.1 CLI Reference, config system admin user (two-factor-auth); Chapter 13 row *FortiManager supports MFA with FortiToken Cloud*

Prerequisite: A reachable SMTP server (with STARTTLS and an account if it requires authentication)
What it enables: Alert email to the ISSO and administrators, and workflow approval notifications
How to put it in place: An organization mail server, then config system mail; edit <SMTP>; set server <SMTP_IP>; set secure-option starttls; set auth enable; end
Source: FortiManager 8.0.1 CLI Reference, config system mail and config system workflow approval-matrix (mail-server); Chapter 13 row *Alert email (SMTP)*

Prerequisite: SNMPv3 manager configured with the same user, authentication, and privacy settings
What it enables: SNMPv3 queries and notifications with SHA-2 authentication and AES privacy
How to put it in place: The organization network management system, then config system snmp user; edit <USER>; set notify-hosts <NMS_IP>; set queries enable; end
Source: FortiManager 8.0.1 CLI Reference, config system snmp user; Chapter 13 rows *SNMPv3* and *Support higher authentication and encryption for SNMP v3*

Prerequisite: Authoritative NTP servers and their authentication keys
What it enables: Synchronized, authenticated time for the FortiManager's own records
How to put it in place: Organization NTP servers, then config system ntp; config ntpserver; edit 1; set server <NTP_IP>; set authentication enable; set key-type sha256; set key-id <ID>; set key <KEY>; end; end
Source: FortiManager 8.0.1 CLI Reference, config system ntp; Chapter 13 rows *NTP server* and *FortiManager supports NTPv4 with SHA-256 encryption*

Prerequisite: A remote syslog server or SIEM that accepts reliable (TCP) syslog with TLS
What it enables: Off-loading the FortiManager's own event logs
How to put it in place: An organization syslog server or SIEM, then config system syslog; edit <SYSLOG>; set ip <SYSLOG_IP>; set reliable enable; set secure-connection enable; end
Source: FortiManager 8.0.1 CLI Reference, config system syslog and config system locallog syslogd setting; Chapter 13 rows *Sending FortiManager event logs to a syslog server* and *Add TLS-SSL support for local log SYSLOG forwarding*

Prerequisite: A FortiAnalyzer that accepts the FortiManager as a log source
What it enables: Real-time off-loading of the FortiManager's own event logs to a FortiAnalyzer
How to put it in place: An organization FortiAnalyzer with the FortiManager registered and authorized as a log source (Chapter 12, P1)
Source: FortiManager 8.0.1 CLI Reference, config system locallog fortianalyzer setting; Chapter 13 row *Sending FortiManager event logs to FortiAnalyzer*

Prerequisite: An SFTP server and account for backups and firmware images
What it enables: Scheduled and on-demand configuration backups, the backup before an upgrade, and loading firmware from the CLI
How to put it in place: An organization SFTP server; the backup runs execute backup all-settings sftp <IP:PORT> <FILE> <USER> <PASSWORD>
Source: FortiManager 8.0.1 CLI Reference, execute backup, execute restore image, and config system backup all-settings; Chapter 13 rows *Scheduled configuration backup*, *On-demand configuration backup*, and *FortiManager firmware upgrade*

Prerequisite: The external system a Fabric connector reaches (for example FortiClient EMS, or an SDN platform such as Cisco ACI), with an API account
What it enables: EMS tags in ZTNA policies and the EMS connector settings installed on FortiGates, and dynamic firewall addresses imported through SDN connectors
How to put it in place: An account on the external system for FortiManager, then the connector in GUI: Policy & Objects (Fabric Connectors)
Source: FortiManager 7.0 New Features Guide, "FortiManager centrally manages ZTNA policies using tags retrieved from EMS server via Fabric Connector - 7.0.3" ("Creating an EMS connector on FortiManager"); FortiManager 7.4 New Features Guide, "Import from an SDN connector IPv6 firewall address type 7.4.3" and "Cisco ACI connector supports IPv6 firewall address import 7.4.3"

Prerequisite: A FortiSASE entitlement in the same FortiCloud account as the FortiManager, and the FortiSASE connector enabled
What it enables: FortiSASE as a managed device, and policy package installation to FortiSASE
How to put it in place: Add the FortiSASE entitlement to the FortiManager's FortiCloud account, then enable the connector in GUI: Fabric View > Fabric Connector
Source: FortiManager 7.4 New Features Guide, "FortiManager integration with FortiSASE controller 7.4.8" (prerequisite steps: a valid FortiSASE entitlement in the FortiCloud account, and the FortiManager in the same account) and "Central policy management and synchronization for FortiSASE 7.4.8"

Prerequisite: Console access to the FortiManager (serial console, or the hypervisor console of a VM)
What it enables: Enabling FIPS-CC mode, which is available only from the console
How to put it in place: A console connection, then config system fips; set status enable; end
Source: FortiManager 8.0.1 CLI Reference, config system fips (FIPS mode can only be enabled via console); Chapter 13 row *FIPS-CC mode*

Prerequisite: A FortiManager hardware appliance; for TPM protection, one of the hardware models that has a Trusted Platform Module (TPM)
What it enables: TPM protection of the private data encryption key, and USB port control
How to put it in place: Choose the model from the FortiManager Data Sheet (TPM support); a FortiManager-VM has neither
Source: FortiManager 7.2 New Features Guide, "TPM hardware module 7.2.2" (only select hardware models have a TPM; see the FortiManager Data Sheet); FortiManager 8.0 New Features Guide, "Option to disable USB ports on FortiManager hardware 8.0.1"

Prerequisite: A FortiManager-VM in Microsoft Azure, assigned to an Azure enhanced backup policy
What it enables: VM backups with Azure's enhanced backup policy
How to put it in place: In Azure, assign the FortiManager VM to an enhanced backup policy (see the Microsoft documentation)
Source: FortiManager 7.4 New Features Guide, "FortiManager supports backups using Azure's enhanced backup policy 7.4.2"

Prerequisite: A FortiCloud account with the FortiManager registered in FortiCare
What it enables: FortiCloud SSO for administrators, and VM license activation
How to put it in place: Register the unit in FortiCloud, and check it in GUI: System Settings > Dashboard > License Information
Source: FortiManager 7.0 New Features Guide, "Admins can use a SAML SSO FortiCloud account to log in to FortiManager" (the FortiManager must first be registered on FortiCloud) and "FortiManager VM licenses" (licensing requires FortiCloud)

Prerequisite: A valid FortiCare support contract: the Firmware & General Updates entitlement, and FortiCare Premium or Elite
What it enables: Upgrades to a higher major or minor release, and FortiGuard downloads (7.4.9 and later)
How to put it in place: Purchase and register the contract in FortiCloud; check with diagnose fmupdate dbcontract and diagnose license list
Source: FortiManager 7.4 New Features Guide, "Prevent FortiManagers with an expired support contract from upgrading to a major or minor firmware release" and "FortiGuard downloads restricted to FortiManagers with premium or elite support subscriptions 7.4.9"
